Data and information

Unit 2 · Week 1 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the database foundations chapter, equipment-loans-flat.csv, database-foundations-workbook.md and database-foundations-answers.md. Use paper or a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL installation or student account is needed. Use the fixed reporting date of 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Data and information

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Introduce the equipment desk scenario. Use loan records to explain which items are overdue. Activities are ungraded. Use only the supplied fictional loan records. Suggested timings are flexible. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

2. The equipment desk question

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual recall, then partner explanation

Allow quiet thinking before discussion. Required facts include LoanID, DueDate, Returned and the reporting date. The item identifier is also needed to name the equipment. A due date alone cannot establish overdue status. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

3. A record needs context

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and discussion

These individual values are data. The conclusion that L001 is overdue is information derived from them using a stated rule. False is a text representation in the CSV and must be interpreted or converted appropriately when importing. The reporting date is fixed for this exercise, regardless of the actual date. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

4. Data, information and the overdue rule

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with student predictions

Model L001: Returned=False, due 6 April, so active and overdue. Then model L002: Returned=False, due 8 April, so active but not overdue. Emphasise strictly before. Dates alone do not supply the full answer. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

5. Four loans to compare

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

Partners apply both checks before revealing results. L001 and L006 are overdue. L002 is due today. L003 has been returned. Swap the explaining role after two rows. This table is a four-row extract, not the complete six-loan dataset. All dates are in 2026. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

6. The full six-loan report

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 1–4. Four active loans: L001, L002, L004 and L006. Two overdue loans: L001 and L006. Students should record the date and rule beside the counts. Do not remove L005 merely because E02 also occurs in L002. Offer the model as support, then ask for an independent explanation. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

7. A date is only one part

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Choice and explanation

B follows the stated rule. Ask learners to name both conditions: an unreturned item and a due date before the reporting date. Collect reasons without recording scores. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

8. Data, rule and conclusion

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Example data: L001 has Returned=False and DueDate=2026-04-06. Example information: two loans are overdue on 8 April under the stated rule. If L003 were incorrectly recorded as unreturned, the report would wrongly include it. Correct calculations still depend on accurate records. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.
